title: Wersestadion — Grokipedia
content: The **Wersestadion** is a multi-use stadium located in Ahlen, Germany, primarily used for football matches and serving as the home ground for the fifth-tier club Rot Weiss Ahlen.](#ref-1) With a total capacity of 12,500 spectators—including 4,000 covered seats and 8,500 standing places (6,000 of which are covered)—it features a natural grass pitch equipped with undersoil heating and no running track.](#ref-1) Originally established in the 1940s as the Glückaufkampfbahn on its current site along the Werse River, the venue was redeveloped and renamed Wersestadion in 1997, with the stadium structure built that year under the ownership of Rot Weiss Ahlen.](#ref-2)](#ref-1) The club itself was founded in 1996 through a merger of TuS Ahlen and Blau-Weiß Ahlen, initially operating as LR Ahlen before adopting its current name by the 2007/08 season.](#ref-3) Throughout its history, Wersestadion has been central to Rot Weiss Ahlen's development of young talent, notably hosting the early careers of players who achieved international prominence.

title: Ems River
content: # Ems River. Also referred to as *Eems* in Dutch, the Ems is a 225.2-mile-long river that flows through the North Rhine-Westphalia, and Lower Saxony states in the northwestern portion of Germany. The river drains into Dollart Bay, which forms a part of the Wadden Sea between the northern portions of the Netherlands and Germany. The exact course of the state boundary that passes through the Ems estuary between East Friesland’s Lower Saxon area and Netherland’s Groningen province was a subject of serious boundary dispute between the two nations. The Ems River begins its journey as a brook from the southern slopes of the Teutoburg Forest close to the cozy town of Schloß Holte-Stukenbrock in Gütersloh district in the German State of North Rhine-Westphalia. The Ems River drains into Dollart Bay immediately south of the German city of Emden and continues its journey toward the Dutch town of Delfzijl as a tidal river.

title: Rot Weiss Ahlen - Wikipedia
content: # Rot Weiss Ahlen. **Rot Weiss Ahlen** is a German football club based in Ahlen, North Rhine-Westphalia. Until 2006 the club was known as **LR Ahlen** for its major sponsor, but underwent a name change when the sponsor withdrew its support after the team was relegated to the Regionalliga (III) in that year. In each of the following three seasons *TuS* earned another championship and promotion; out of the Landesliga, through the Verbandsliga Westfalen-Nordost (V) and Oberliga Westfalen (IV), leading to the Regionalliga West/Südwest (III). *Leichtathletik Rasensport Ahlen* was formed on 1 June 1996 when *TuS Ahlen* merged with *Blau-Weiß Ahlen* to begin play in the Regionalliga West/Südwest in 1996–97. After being relegated *LR Ahlen* lost the support of its major sponsor and underwent a name change to become *Rot Weiss Ahlen* on 31 May 2006.
